questions.prompt: Week 34 · The Constitution in Practice: Federalism and the Courts: What is the strongest method for evaluating “Reading a Supreme Court Case”?
choices: Accept the source because it was created during the period.
Reject the source if it has a perspective or purpose.
Compare it with independent evidence and evaluate origin, purpose, context, value, and limits.
Use only the most memorable statement.
questions.explanation: Historical evidence is evaluated through sourcing, contextualization, corroboration, and attention to limitations.
questions.skill: Unit 8 · Constitutional and Civic Synthesis · Week 34

questions.prompt: A federalism case map shows different state laws, federal rules, court rulings, and implementation dates. What is the strongest analysis?
choices: Distinguish which level of government acted, when legal authority changed, and how implementation varied instead of treating the map as one uniform national policy.
Assume a federal court ruling immediately produced identical state practice.
Treat every state law as independent of federal constitutional limits.
Use the latest boundary layer as proof of legal agreement.
questions.explanation: Federalism analysis depends on jurisdiction, timing, legal authority, and implementation, not merely geographic variation.
